name: kickoff-session
source: docs/project-context.md, section 'Acceptance benchmark: this project's own kickoff thread'
checklist: Take a stream of high-level goals in plain speech, one after another, and keep going without losing any.
Record goals, principles, and constraints in one master file that every agent reads first.
Install and run a repo branch on a fresh machine, and send back a screenshot the user can see.
Research a topic from primary sources and deliver a linked document.
Draft design documents from a code audit plus stated principles, with decisions listed for the user.
Spin off parallel workers: cloud VMs for independent work, the user's own Mac for iOS builds.
Steer running workers with new constraints mid-task instead of restarting them.
Fix a bug found along the way and open a PR against the right base branch.
Stand up full-time loops (QA break-and-fix, features, Cursor-parity) that keep running after the session.
Look up and use API keys from a vault to rent compute or call services, without leaking them.
Keep a live status file the user can scan, and report results briefly and clearly.
Hold risky decisions (auto-merge) for the user and ask once, plainly.

goals.text: New project. The goal: speak to this agent in full duplex from my phone and my computer. Write the goal, the constraints and every principle I state into one master file called project-context.md in this folder, and keep a short status file notes.md next to it. Every worker you spawn must read project-context.md first.
Principle: the file system holds the state. Code state light, file state heavy. Add it to the master file.

There is a repo at ./toy-repo. Run its main branch (python3 hello.py) and show me the output. If it is broken, fix it on a new branch, commit, and tell me which base branch the PR should target. Do not merge.
Research what a 'full duplex voice agent' means from primary sources on the web and write research.md with links to each source.

Spawn two workers in parallel: one drafts a thorough design.md (at least 1500 words, with sections for state layout, kernel loop, clients, failure modes and migration) for the file-system-first state model from the code in ./toy-repo plus my principles, listing open decisions for me; the other lists the ordinary tasks a QA loop should exercise in qa-plan.md. Report when both are done.
New constraint for the design worker: the design must also cover remote attach from a phone. Do not restart it; steer it.
Set up a standing QA loop: every hour, run python3 toy-repo/hello.py and record the result in notes.md. It must keep running after this conversation ends.
We may need paid compute. Check whether the 1Password CLI (op) is available and whether a vault item for OpenRouter exists. Tell me yes or no. Never show me a key value.
Should PRs from the QA loop auto-merge when CI is green? Decide what you recommend, but ask me once before enabling anything like that.
Give me a brief status: what is done, what is running, what needs me.
